subject: StellarNet TAM coverage, handoff matrix & exec notification thresholds
messages:
From: Anna Lopez <anna@stellarnet.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Halvorsen <markus@stellarnet.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Sep 2027 13:12:00 -0400
Subject: RFP follow-up: TAM coverage & escalation expectations

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the materials in the RFP response so far. A couple of follow-ups from our SRE and procurement teams so we can close our support appendix quickly:

1) Coverage hours and handoffs: we need a simple matrix that shows guaranteed coverage windows (US / EU / APAC) and the on-call handoff times (local TZs) for TAM/Support engineering. Are your TAMs following a 24x7 on-call rotation or is it a follow-the-sun model with tiered escalation?

2) P0/P1 escalation SLAs: what are your target notification and response windows for P0 vs P1 (initial ack, engineer engagement, exec notification)? We need clear thresholds for when StellarNet execs will be notified.

3) Auditability: do you provide a runbook/audit trail of incident comms (email/Slack/ticket) for compliance? We'd like examples or a schema for exported incident timelines.

4) Handoff artifacts: could you share a sample handoff roster (names/titles/timezones/primary contact method) and the handoff checklist you use when shifting between regions?

If you can attach a short spreadsheet and any SLA exhibit that maps to the RFP, that would be ideal. We have a call with procurement on Wednesday so if possible please send by Tuesday EOD.

Thanks,
Anna
Anna Lopez
Head of Site Reliability
StellarNet Inc.
[External Attachment: stellarnet-rfp-summary.pdf]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Anna Lopez <anna@stellarnet.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Sep 2027 15:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: RFP follow-up: TAM coverage & escalation expectations

Hi Anna — thanks for the clear list. See answers inline and I've attached two artifacts that should map directly into your procurement appendix: the SLA exhibit (PDF) and a confidential TAM handoff roster (xlsx).

1) Coverage hours and handoffs
- Model: follow-the-sun for incident response, with regional TAM primary ownership and a global on-call pool for overflow.
- US coverage (primary): 07:00-19:00 ET local account coverage; global on-call covers nights.
- EU coverage (primary): 08:00-18:00 CET local account coverage; APAC overlap handled by Asia Pacific TAMs 09:00-19:00 SGT.
- Handoff cadence: formal handoff at 09:00 UTC and 21:00 UTC daily where the outgoing TAM sends the handoff checklist to the next owner, posts the summary to the shared incident channel, and updates the roster.

2) P0/P1 escalation SLAs
- Initial notification (automated): within 2 minutes for P0 via PagerDuty and email.
- Acknowledgement (human): P0 within 15 minutes, P1 within 60 minutes.
- Engineer engagement: P0 within 30 minutes on average (target), P1 within 4 hours.
- Exec notification: triggered for P0 if incident remains unresolved after 2 hours or upon customer request; for P1 execs are notified when business impact crosses agreed revenue/availability thresholds (specified in SLA exhibit).

3) Auditability
- We export incident timelines from our incident platform (ticket + Slack thread + PD audit) as a single artifact. The runbook includes message timestamps, responder names, actions taken, and links to artifacts. See the example schema in the SLA exhibit and sample timeline in the attached roster workbook.

4) Handoff artifacts
- Attached: tam-handoff-roster.xlsx (columns: name, role, region, primary contact, PD escalation id, local tz, shift start, shift end, backup).
- Handoff checklist (tab in workbook): summary, active incidents, open actions with owners, risk notes, planned maintenance, upcoming business-critical events.

Attachments included:
- redwood-support-sla-exhibit.pdf (SLA thresholds, notification logic, credits/metrics)
- tam-handoff-roster.xlsx (sample roster + handoff checklist)

If you'd like, Priyom (cc'd) can provide the SOC2/audit export format and the typical incident export we provide for customer audits. Happy to hop on a call to walk procurement through the exhibit Tuesday morning — what time works?

Best,

Kimberly Park
Head of Customer Success — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-support-sla-exhibit.pdf] [Attachment: tam-handoff-roster.xlsx]

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: RFP follow-up: TAM coverage & escalation expectations

Thanks Anna / Kimberly — adding a few specifics from the ops/audit side:

> On Sun, 12 Sep 2027 15:05:00 -0400 Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com> wrote:
> > 2) P0/P1 escalation SLAs
> > - Initial notification (automated): within 2 minutes for P0 via PagerDuty and email.
> > - Acknowledgement (human): P0 within 15 minutes, P1 within 60 minutes.

For clarity and for your compliance team: the incident export we provide contains the following fields as separate records — incident id, timestamps (created/ack/resolve), participant list (names + roles), channel transcripts (Slack/Email), PD incident log, and attachments (config diffs, stack traces). We also redact customer-sensitive text by default and can provide a signed NDA'd bundle for full logs.

Regarding exec notifications: our default threshold for auto-escalation to executive ops is 2 hours for P0 if no containment; we will include a manual opt-in in the SLA for immediate exec notification if StellarNet prefers.

Finally, about the roster spreadsheet: the PD escalation id column maps to PagerDuty schedule entries and is best-effort for contractor TAMs (we include a backup contact always).

If procurement needs the sample export format, I'm attaching the JSON schema (included in the Drive link Kimberly shared) and can export a redacted example on request.

Cheers,
Priyom
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
